doc_screened_files.reason: This is the main coercion engine for HIR type checking, and the bug manifests as an E0308 mismatch on a simple initializer that should coerce cleanly to `Pin<Box<()>>`. A bad coercion path is the most direct fit for the "expected `Pin<X>` found `Pin<X>`" symptom.

`Box::pin(())` is a call expression, so the callee/argument checking path is involved before the final assignment to the annotated local. If pin ergonomics is mis-resolving or mis-typing the call result, this is one of the first places it can go wrong.

The failing code is an expression used as a let initializer, and this module owns the main expression type-checking flow that feeds expected types into coercion. A bug here could surface as a bogus same-type mismatch even when the callee itself is well-typed.

This file checks body-level signatures and return/coercion expectations for typed bodies. The trace shows normal typeck activity on `foo` and `main`, so a bug in how the body context is set up could cause the initializer to be compared against the wrong expectation.

This module performs deferred and call-specific checks, including validating function call argument lists and building mismatch diagnostics. Since the failure is triggered by `Box::pin(())`, a bad call-checking path could be producing the misleading E0308.

The error suggests the compiler may be propagating the wrong expected type through the initializer. This file owns the expectation model used during expression checking, so a bug here could make two structurally identical `Pin` types compare as incompatible.

This is the core per-body type-checking state machine, including divergence, normalization, and deferred obligation plumbing. If pin ergonomics interacts with hidden inference state, the failure could come from the shared `FnCtxt` machinery here.

Pin ergonomics is fundamentally about place- and projection-sensitive behavior, so the place-operation layer is a plausible source if special pin-related adjustments are being applied incorrectly. It is less direct than coercion, but still relevant to the feature area.

Type-checking stores coercion and adjustment results here, so a malformed adjustment for a `Pin<Box<_>>` initializer could make the diagnostic report an impossible self-mismatch. This is a likely lower-level site if the bug is in how the coercion is recorded rather than decided.

The same-textual `Pin<_>` mismatch points to a possible relation/normalization bug where two equivalent-looking types are treated as distinct during comparison. This is a broader type-relation fallback suspect if the problem is not in expression-level coercion.
